title: Delta Method
informal: Let $\phi$ be a map between normed spaces that is Fréchet differentiable at $ heta_0$, with continuous linear derivative $\phi^{\prime}$. If the scaling constants satisfy $s_n o\infty$ and $s_n(T_n- heta_0)$ converges weakly to a law $ u$, then — with $T_n$ measurable and $\phi(T_n)$ almost everywhere measurable, so that both sides have laws — the scaled Taylor remainder $s_n igl(\phi(T_n)-\phi( heta_0) igr)-\phi^{\prime} igl(s_n(T_n- heta_0) igr)$ tends to $0$ in probability, and $$s_n igl(\phi(T_n)-\phi( heta_0) igr) ightsquigarrow u\circ(\phi^{\prime})^{-1},$$ the image of $ u$ under the derivative $\phi^{\prime}$.
summary: Weak convergence transports through a differentiable map, with a vanishing first-order Taylor remainder.
leanSignature:
theorem delta_method
    {E F : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
      [SecondCountableTopology E] [CompleteSpace E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [MeasurableSpace F] [BorelSpace F]
      [SecondCountableTopology F] [Nonempty F]
    {P : ∀ k, Measure (Ω k)} [∀ k, IsProbabilityMeasure (P k)]
    {T : ∀ k, Ω k → E} (hT_meas : ∀ k, Measurable (T k))
    {φ : E → F} {φ' : E →L[ℝ] F} {θ₀ : E}
    (hφ : HasFDerivAt φ φ' θ₀)
    (hφT_meas : ∀ k, AEMeasurable (fun ω => φ (T k ω)) (P k))
    {sqn : ℕ → ℝ} (h_sqn : Tendsto sqn atTop atTop)
    {ν : Measure E} [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
    (h_wc : WeakConverges (fun k => (P k).map (fun ω => sqn k • (T k ω - θ₀))) ν) :
    WeakConverges (fun k => (P k).map (fun ω => sqn k • (φ (T k ω) - φ θ₀))) (ν.map φ')
      ∧ TendstoInProbZero P
          (fun k ω => sqn k • (φ (T k ω) - φ θ₀ - φ' (T k ω - θ₀)))
formalizationNotes: Consistency and stochastic boundedness follow from weak convergence; they are not hypotheses. The conclusion includes both weak convergence and the theorem's moreover remainder clause.

hypotheses.label: Fréchet differentiability
hypotheses.note: φ is Fréchet differentiable at θ₀, with continuous linear derivative φ'.

hypotheses.label: measurability
hypotheses.note: T_n is measurable and φ(T_n) is almost everywhere measurable, so both statistics have well-defined laws.

hypotheses.label: diverging scale
hypotheses.note: The scaling constants s_n tend to +∞.

hypotheses.label: weak limit of the input
hypotheses.note: The rescaled centred statistic s_n(T_n − θ₀) converges weakly to the law ν.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: The delta method's systematic use in asymptotic statistics goes back to H. Cramér, *Mathematical Methods of Statistics*, Princeton University Press, 1946, where limit laws of smooth transformations are derived by Taylor expansion.

title: Method-of-Moments Normality
informal: Let $X_1,X_2,\dots$ be independent and identically distributed with law $P$, let $f$ be a measurable $\mathbb R^d$-valued moment function that is square-integrable under $P$, and let the moment map $e$ have a strict derivative $e^{\prime}_{\theta_0}$ at $\theta_0$ that is a continuous linear isomorphism, with $e(\theta_0)=\int f\,dP$. Then there are measurable estimators $\hat\theta_n$ solving the moment equation $e(\hat\theta_n)=\mathbb P_nf:=n^{-1}\sum_{i\le n}f(X_i)$ with probability tending to one, and they satisfy the linear representation $$\sqrt n(\hat\theta_n-\theta_0)=(e^{\prime}_{\theta_0})^{-1}\Bigl(\sqrt n\bigl(\mathbb P_nf-\textstyle\int f\,dP\bigr)\Bigr)+o_P(1),$$ so that $\sqrt n(\hat\theta_n-\theta_0)\rightsquigarrow N\bigl(0,\,(e^{\prime}_{\theta_0})^{-1}\operatorname{Cov}_P(f)\,\bigl((e^{\prime}_{\theta_0})^{-1}\bigr)^{\mathsf T}\bigr)$.
summary: A measurable solution of the moment equation exists asymptotically and is asymptotically linear and Gaussian.
leanSignature:
theorem method_of_moments_normality {d : ℕ}
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    {f : Ω → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)} (hf_meas : Measurable f) (hf_L2 : MemLp f 2 P)
    {e : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)}
    {e' : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) ≃L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)}
    {θ₀ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)}
    (he : HasStrictFDerivAt e (e' : _ →L[ℝ] _) θ₀)
    (hμ : e θ₀ = ∫ x, f x ∂P)
    {Ξ : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ξ] {μ : Measure Ξ} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    {X : ℕ → Ξ → Ω} (hX_meas : ∀ i, Measurable (X i))
    (hX_indep : iIndepFun X μ)
    (hX_id : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ)
    (hX_law : μ.map (X 0) = P) :
    ∃ θhat : ℕ → Ξ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d),
      (∀ n, Measurable (θhat n)) ∧
      Tendsto (fun n => μ.real {ξ | e (θhat n ξ) = empiricalMoment f n X ξ}) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      TendstoInProbZero (fun _ : ℕ => μ)
        (fun n ξ => Real.sqrt n • (θhat n ξ - θ₀)
          - (↑e'.symm : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
              (Real.sqrt n • (empiricalMoment f n X ξ - ∫ x, f x ∂P))) ∧
      WeakConverges (fun n => μ.map (fun ξ => Real.sqrt n • (θhat n ξ - θ₀)))
        (multivariateGaussian 0 (momentLimitCov P f e'))
formalizationNotes: Estimator existence and measurability are conclusions. Consistency and tightness are derived from the empirical-moment CLT.

hypotheses.label: square-integrable moments
hypotheses.note: f is measurable and square-integrable under P.

hypotheses.label: invertible derivative
hypotheses.note: e has a strict derivative at θ₀ which is a continuous linear isomorphism, hence invertible.

hypotheses.label: moment identity
hypotheses.note: The moment map matches the true moment: e(θ₀) = ∫ f dP.

hypotheses.label: i.i.d. sample from P
hypotheses.note: The observations are independent, identically distributed, with marginal law P.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: The method of moments goes back to K. Pearson, "Contributions to the mathematical theory of evolution," *Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London A* **185** (1894), 71–110. Its asymptotic normality combines the central limit theorem with the delta method as developed by H. Cramér, *Mathematical Methods of Statistics*, Princeton University Press, 1946.

title: M-Estimator Consistency
informal: Let $M_n$ be random criterion functions on a metric parameter set $\Theta$ and $M$ a deterministic limit criterion. If a measurable envelope $U_n$ dominates the uniform error, $\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}|M_n(\theta)-M(\theta)|\le U_n$, and $U_n\to_P0$; if $\theta_0$ is a well-separated maximum of $M$, i.e. for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\eta>0$ with $M(\theta)\le M(\theta_0)-\eta$ whenever $d(\theta,\theta_0)\ge\varepsilon$; and if $\hat\theta_n$ almost maximizes $M_n$, in the sense that $M_n(\hat\theta_n)\ge M_n(\theta_0)-R_n$ for a slack $R_n\to_P0$; then $\hat\theta_n\to_P\theta_0$.
summary: Uniform criterion convergence plus a separated population maximum makes every near-maximizer consistent.
leanSignature:
theorem mEstimator_consistent
    {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω}
    {Θ : Type*} [MetricSpace Θ]
    {Mn : ℕ → Ω → Θ → ℝ} {M : Θ → ℝ} {θ₀ : Θ} {θhat : ℕ → Ω → Θ}
    {U R : ℕ → Ω → ℝ}
    (hU_dom : ∀ n ω θ, |Mn n ω θ - M θ| ≤ U n ω)
    (hU_conv : TendstoInMeasure P U atTop (fun _ => (0 : ℝ)))
    (hsep : ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ η > (0 : ℝ), ∀ θ, ε ≤ dist θ θ₀ → M θ ≤ M θ₀ - η)
    (hnear : ∀ n ω, Mn n ω θ₀ - R n ω ≤ Mn n ω (θhat n ω))
    (hR_conv : TendstoInMeasure P R atTop (fun _ => (0 : ℝ))) :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), Tendsto (fun n => P {ω | ε ≤ dist (θhat n ω) θ₀}) atTop (𝓝 0)
formalizationNotes: The envelope encodes the uniform error without requiring measurability of a supremum. Neither estimator measurability nor a probability-measure instance is required.

hypotheses.label: uniform convergence
hypotheses.note: A measurable envelope dominates the uniform criterion error sup_θ |M_n(θ) − M(θ)| and tends to zero in probability.

hypotheses.label: separated maximum
hypotheses.note: For every ε > 0 there is η > 0 with M(θ) ≤ M(θ₀) − η whenever θ is at distance at least ε from θ₀.

hypotheses.label: near maximization
hypotheses.note: The maximizing slack R_n in M_n(θ̂_n) ≥ M_n(θ₀) − R_n tends to zero in probability.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: The argmax route to consistency originates with A. Wald, "Note on the consistency of the maximum likelihood estimate," *The Annals of Mathematical Statistics* **20** (1949), 595–601. P. J. Huber extended it to general M-estimators in "The behavior of maximum likelihood estimates under nonstandard conditions," *Fifth Berkeley Symposium* (1967), and A. W. van der Vaart and J. A. Wellner developed the empirical-process formulation in *Weak Convergence and Empirical Processes*, Springer, 1996.

title: Z-Estimator Consistency
informal: Let $\Psi_n$ be random maps from a metric parameter set $\Theta$ into a normed space and $\Psi$ a deterministic limit. If a measurable envelope $U_n$ dominates the uniform error, $\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\|\Psi_n(\theta)-\Psi(\theta)\|\le U_n$, and $U_n\to_P0$; if $\Psi(\theta_0)=0$ and the zero is separated, i.e. for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\eta>0$ with $\|\Psi(\theta)\|\ge\eta$ whenever $d(\theta,\theta_0)\ge\varepsilon$; and if $\|\Psi_n(\hat\theta_n)\|\to_P0$; then $\hat\theta_n\to_P\theta_0$.
summary: Uniform estimating-equation convergence and zero separation imply consistency of near-roots.

    {Θ : Type*} [MetricSpace Θ]

    {U : ℕ → Ω → ℝ}
    (hU_dom : ∀ n ω θ, ‖Ψn n ω θ - Ψ θ‖ ≤ U n ω)
    (hU_conv : TendstoInMeasure P U atTop (fun _ => (0 : ℝ)))
    (hΨ0 : Ψ θ₀ = 0)
    (hsep : ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ η > (0 : ℝ), ∀ θ, ε ≤ dist θ θ₀ → η ≤ ‖Ψ θ‖)
    (hnear : TendstoInMeasure P (fun n ω => ‖Ψn n ω (θhat n ω)‖) atTop (fun _ => (0 : ℝ))) :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), Tendsto (fun n => P {ω | ε ≤ dist (θhat n ω) θ₀}) atTop (𝓝 0)
formalizationNotes: Uniform convergence is expressed through a measurable envelope, and estimator measurability is not assumed.

hypotheses.label: uniform convergence
hypotheses.note: A measurable envelope dominates sup_θ ‖Ψ_n(θ) − Ψ(θ)‖ and tends to zero in probability.

hypotheses.label: identified separated zero
hypotheses.note: Ψ vanishes at θ₀, and for every ε > 0 the norm ‖Ψ(θ)‖ stays above a positive constant at distance at least ε from θ₀.

hypotheses.label: approximate root
hypotheses.note: The estimating function evaluated at the estimator, ‖Ψ_n(θ̂_n)‖, tends to zero in probability.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: Estimators defined by vanishing criterion functions descend from the classical analysis of likelihood equations in H. Cramér, *Mathematical Methods of Statistics*, Princeton University Press, 1946, and P. J. Huber's work on M-estimators in 1964 and 1967.

title: Monotone One-Dimensional Z-Estimator Consistency
informal: Let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a set containing $\theta_0$ and every $\hat\theta_n$, and order-connected: whenever it contains two points it contains the whole interval between them, and let $\Psi_n:\Theta\to\mathbb R$ be random functions that are nondecreasing on $\Theta$. Assume $\Psi_n(\theta)\to_P\Psi(\theta)$ for each fixed $\theta\in\Theta$, and the limit changes sign strictly at $\theta_0$: $\Psi(\theta)<0$ for $\theta<\theta_0$ and $\Psi(\theta)>0$ for $\theta>\theta_0$. If the estimators take values in $\Theta$ and $\Psi_n(\hat\theta_n)\to_P0$, then $\hat\theta_n\to_P\theta_0$.
summary: Pointwise convergence and monotonicity turn a strict sign change into consistency of approximate roots.
leanSignature:
theorem oneDim_monotone_zEstimator_consistent
    {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω}
    {Θ : Set ℝ} (hΘ : Θ.OrdConnected)
    {Ψn : ℕ → Ω → ℝ → ℝ} {Ψ : ℝ → ℝ} {θ₀ : ℝ} {θhat : ℕ → Ω → ℝ}
    (hθ₀ : θ₀ ∈ Θ)
    (hθhat : ∀ n ω, θhat n ω ∈ Θ)
    (hmono : ∀ n ω, MonotoneOn (Ψn n ω) Θ)
    (hptwise : ∀ θ ∈ Θ, TendstoInMeasure P (fun n ω => Ψn n ω θ) atTop (fun _ => Ψ θ))
    (hnear : TendstoInMeasure P (fun n ω => Ψn n ω (θhat n ω)) atTop (fun _ => (0 : ℝ)))
    (hsign_lt : ∀ θ ∈ Θ, θ < θ₀ → Ψ θ < 0)
    (hsign_gt : ∀ θ ∈ Θ, θ₀ < θ → 0 < Ψ θ) :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), Tendsto (fun n => P {ω | ε ≤ |θhat n ω - θ₀|}) atTop (𝓝 0)
formalizationNotes: Works for a general measure and needs no estimator measurability. Order-connectedness handles boundary cases without an interior-point assumption.

hypotheses.label: order-connected domain
hypotheses.note: The true parameter and every estimator value belong to the order-connected set Θ.

hypotheses.label: monotonicity
hypotheses.note: Each random estimating function is nondecreasing on Θ.

hypotheses.label: pointwise limit with strict sign change
hypotheses.note: Ψ_n(θ) → Ψ(θ) in probability for each fixed θ, and Ψ is strictly negative left of θ₀ and strictly positive right of θ₀.

hypotheses.label: approximate root
hypotheses.note: The estimating function evaluated at the estimator tends to zero in probability.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: Monotone estimating equations arise in P. J. Huber, "Robust estimation of a location parameter," *The Annals of Mathematical Statistics* **35** (1964), 73–101.

title: Continuous One-Dimensional Z-Estimator Consistency
informal: Let $\Psi_n:\Theta\to\mathbb R$ be random functions on $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R$, where $\Theta$ is a neighbourhood of $\theta_0$. Assume each $\Psi_n$ is continuous on $\Theta$ and has $\hat\theta_n$ as its only zero there: $\Psi_n(\theta)=0$ with $\theta\in\Theta$ forces $\theta=\hat\theta_n$, and $\Psi_n(\theta)\to_P\Psi(\theta)$ for each fixed $\theta\in\Theta$, with $\Psi(\theta)<0$ for $\theta<\theta_0$ and $\Psi(\theta)>0$ for $\theta>\theta_0$. Then $\hat\theta_n\to_P\theta_0$.
summary: Continuity, uniqueness, pointwise convergence, and a strict sign change imply consistency of the one-dimensional root.
leanSignature:
theorem oneDim_continuous_zEstimator_consistent
    {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω}
    {Θ : Set ℝ}
    {Ψn : ℕ → Ω → ℝ → ℝ} {Ψ : ℝ → ℝ} {θ₀ : ℝ} {θhat : ℕ → Ω → ℝ}
    (hθ₀_int : Θ ∈ 𝓝 θ₀)

    (hunique : ∀ n ω θ, θ ∈ Θ → Ψn n ω θ = 0 → θ = θhat n ω)
    (hptwise : ∀ θ ∈ Θ, TendstoInMeasure P (fun n ω => Ψn n ω θ) atTop (fun _ => Ψ θ))
    (hsign_lt : ∀ θ ∈ Θ, θ < θ₀ → Ψ θ < 0)
    (hsign_gt : ∀ θ ∈ Θ, θ₀ < θ → 0 < Ψ θ) :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), Tendsto (fun n => P {ω | ε ≤ |θhat n ω - θ₀|}) atTop (𝓝 0)
formalizationNotes: Interiority is explicit and necessary for this continuous route. The theorem does not separately assume that $\hat\theta_n$ lies in Θ or is measurable.

hypotheses.label: interior truth
hypotheses.note: Θ is a neighbourhood of θ₀.

hypotheses.label: continuity and unique zero
hypotheses.note: Each Ψ_n is continuous on Θ and every zero of Ψ_n in Θ equals the estimator θ̂_n.

hypotheses.label: pointwise limit with strict sign change
hypotheses.note: Ψ_n(θ) → Ψ(θ) in probability for each fixed θ, and Ψ is strictly negative left of θ₀ and strictly positive right of θ₀.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: The use of continuous estimating equations in asymptotic estimation is classical; see H. Cramér, *Mathematical Methods of Statistics*, Princeton University Press, 1946.

title: Wald Consistency on Compact Sets
informal: Let $Q$ be the observation law and let $m_\theta$ be an extended-real criterion on a metric parameter space. Define $M(\theta)$ as the one-sided expectation of $m_\theta$, allowing an infinite negative part. Assume the criteria never take the value $+\infty$; for every $\theta$, the map $\eta\mapsto m_\eta(x)$ is upper semicontinuous at $\theta$ for $Q$-almost every $x$; and around every $\theta$, shrinking-ball suprema of the criterion are measurable and have finite positive-part expectation. Suppose $\theta_0$ maximizes $M$, $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ are measurable, independent, and identically distributed with law $Q$, and $\hat\theta_n$ nearly maximizes the empirical criterion, up to a real remainder $R_n$ with $R_n\to_P0$. Then for every compact set $K$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, the probability that $\hat\theta_n\in K$ while its distance from the population argmax set is at least $\varepsilon$ tends to zero.
summary: A near-maximizer of an upper-semicontinuous one-sided empirical criterion cannot remain in a compact set away from the population argmax set.

    {X Ω Θ : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MetricSpace Θ]
    (Q : Measure X) [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]
    (ℙ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure ℙ]
    (Xs : ℕ → Ω → X) (m : Θ → X → EReal) (θ₀ : Θ)
    (θhat : ℕ → Ω → Θ) (R : ℕ → Ω → ℝ)
    (hm_top : ∀ θ x, m θ x ≠ ⊤)
    (husc : ∀ θ, ∀ᵐ x ∂Q, UpperSemicontinuousAt (fun η => m η x) θ)
    (hlocal : ∀ θ, ∃ ρ > 0, ∀ r, 0 < r → r ≤ ρ →
      Measurable (localCriterionSup m θ r) ∧
      (∫⁻ x, (localCriterionSup m θ r x).toENNReal ∂Q) ≠ ∞)
    (hmax : θ₀ ∈ {θ | ∀ η,
      extendedExpectation Q (m η) ≤ extendedExpectation Q (m θ)})
    (hXs_meas : ∀ i, Measurable (Xs i))
    (hXs_indep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun Xs ℙ)
    (hXs_id : ∀ i, ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (Xs i) (Xs 0) ℙ ℙ)
    (hXs_law : ℙ.map (Xs 0) = Q)

    ∀ ε > 0, Tendsto (fun n => ℙ {ω |

hypotheses.label: no positive infinity
hypotheses.note: Every criterion value lies in the extended interval [−∞, ∞).

hypotheses.label: upper semicontinuity
hypotheses.note: At every parameter θ, the criterion is upper semicontinuous in the parameter for Q-almost every observation.

hypotheses.label: integrable local envelopes
hypotheses.note: Sufficiently small local suprema are measurable and have finite positive-part expectation.

hypotheses.label: population maximizer
hypotheses.note: The comparison point θ₀ maximizes the one-sided population expectation.

hypotheses.label: i.i.d. observations
hypotheses.note: The sample coordinates are measurable, independent, identically distributed, and have common law Q.

hypotheses.label: near maximization
hypotheses.note: The empirical criterion at θ̂_n is at least its value at θ₀ minus the remainder R_n.

hypotheses.label: vanishing remainder
hypotheses.note: The near-maximization remainder R_n tends to zero in probability.

hypotheses.label: compact localization
hypotheses.note: K is a compact subset of the parameter space.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: The compact-cover consistency argument descends from A. Wald, "Note on the consistency of the maximum likelihood estimate," *The Annals of Mathematical Statistics* **20** (1949), 595–601.

title: Z-Estimator Asymptotic Normality
informal: Let $\psi_\theta$ be a vector estimating function near $\theta_0$. Assume the derivative matrix $V$ is nonsingular and the local class is Lipschitz with a measurable square-integrable envelope, every estimating function is measurable, the score at $\theta_0$ is centered and square-integrable, and the population equation is Fréchet differentiable at $\theta_0$ with derivative $V$. Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be a measurable independent and identically distributed sample with law $P$. Suppose $\hat\theta_n$ is measurable and consistent, for every $n$ and coordinate $j$, the map $(\xi,x)\mapsto\psi_{\hat\theta_n(\xi),j}(x)$ is jointly measurable, and $\sqrt n\,\mathbb P_n\psi_{\hat\theta_n}$ tends to zero in outer probability, uniformly over coordinates. Then $$\sqrt n(\hat\theta_n-\theta_0)\rightsquigarrow N\left(0,V^{-1}P[\psi_{\theta_0}\psi_{\theta_0}^{\mathsf T}](V^{-1})^{\mathsf T}\right).$$
summary: A consistent approximate Z-root is asymptotically Gaussian under local Lipschitz, differentiability, and L² conditions.

title: M-Estimator Asymptotic Normality
informal: Let $m_\theta$ be measurable criterion functions on $\mathbb R^d$ with a local $L^2$ Lipschitz property, $|m_{\theta_1}(x)-m_{\theta_2}(x)|\le \dot m_{\mathrm{env}}(x)\|\theta_1-\theta_2\|$ on a ball around $\theta_0$ with $\dot m_{\mathrm{env}}$ square-$P$-integrable, and an almost sure derivative $\dot m_{\theta_0}$ at $\theta_0$. title: Z-Estimator Representation with Estimated Nuisance
informal: Let $\psi_{\theta,\eta}$ be measurable estimating functions with $\int\psi_{\theta_0,\eta_0}\,dP=0$ depending on the parameter $\theta\in\mathbb R^k$ and a nuisance $\eta$ in a metric space. Assume the local class $\{\psi_{\theta,\eta}:\|\theta-\theta_0\|<\delta,\ d(\eta,\eta_0)<\delta\}$ is $P$-Donsker and $L^2(P)$-continuous at $(\theta_0,\eta_0)$, i.e. $\int(\psi_{\theta,\eta}-\psi_{\theta_0,\eta_0})^2\,dP\to0$ as $(\theta,\eta)\to(\theta_0,\eta_0)$, and $\theta\mapsto\int\psi_{\theta,\eta}\,dP$ is Fréchet differentiable at $\theta_0$ uniformly over $\eta$ near $\eta_0$, with derivative matrix $V_\eta$ continuous at $\eta_0$ and $V_{\eta_0}$ nonsingular. If the observations are i.i.d. $P$, $\hat\theta_n\to_P\theta_0$ and $\hat\eta_n\to_P\eta_0$, and $\sqrt n\,\mathbb P_n\psi_{\hat\theta_n,\hat\eta_n}\to0$ in outer probability, then $$\sqrt n(\hat\theta_n-\theta_0)=-V_{\eta_0}^{-1}\Bigl(\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i\le n}\psi_{\theta_0,\eta_0}(X_i)+\sqrt n\int\psi_{\theta_0,\hat\eta_n}\,dP\Bigr)+o_P(1),$$ the remainder being $o_P(1)$ after division by $1+\sqrt n\,\bigl\|\int\psi_{\theta_0,\hat\eta_n}\,dP\bigr\|$. The second term inside the brackets is the drift contributed by estimating the nuisance; it vanishes when $\eta_0$ is known.
summary: A Z-estimator with an estimated nuisance has the weighted linear representation including the nuisance drift term.

title: MLE Consistency from KL Identifiability
citation: van der Vaart (1998), Thm 5.7 route + Lem 5.35
informal: Let $\{p_\theta\}$ be a family of genuine probability densities relative to $\mu$ whose parametrization is identifiable at $\theta_0$: if $p_\theta\,d\mu=p_{\theta_0}\,d\mu$ then $\theta=\theta_0$. Assume $M$ is upper semicontinuous and some superlevel set $\{\theta:M(\theta)\ge c\}$ with $c. summary: KL identifiability, compact separation, uniform convergence, and exact likelihood maximization imply MLE consistency.

title: Rate of Convergence for M-Estimators, Corrected Form

title: Argmax Theorem
informal: Let $M_n$ be stochastic processes on changing sets $H_n$ and let $M$ be a limit process on $H$. summary: Joint convergence of localized suprema and a well-separated limit maximizer imply outer weak convergence of argmax estimators.

    (hnear : ∀ n ω h, h ∈ Hn n →
      Mn n ω h ≤ Mn n ω (hhatn n ω) + r n ω)
    (hcontinuous : ∀ ω, Continuous (M ω))
    (hunique : ∀ ω h, h ∈ H → h ≠ hhat ω → M ω h < M ω (hhat ω))
    (hMnBounded : ∀ n ω (K : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))), IsCompact K →
      Memℓp (fun h : K => Mn n ω h) ∞)
    (hLocalMeas : ∀ (K : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) (hK : IsCompact K),

        (continuous_memℓp_infty_on_compact (M ω) K (hcontinuous ω) hK)))

        (fun n ω => ForMathlib.restrictToLinfOn K (Mn n ω) (hMnBounded n ω K hK))

hypotheses.label: set convergence
hypotheses.note: The changing index sets converge to the limit index set.

hypotheses.label: unique maximizer
hypotheses.note: Every continuous limit path has the designated unique maximizer on the limit set.

hypotheses.label: local process convergence
hypotheses.note: Restrictions to every compact set converge weakly in the uniform norm.

hypotheses.label: near maximization
hypotheses.note: The sample maximizers are within a nonnegative vanishing remainder of all competing values.

hypotheses.label: uniform tightness
hypotheses.note: The sample maximizers lie in a compact set with arbitrarily high outer probability, uniformly in n.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: The systematic empirical-process treatment, including changing-index-set and entropy methods, is developed by A. W. van der Vaart and J. A. Wellner, *Weak Convergence and Empirical Processes*, Springer, 1996.

formalizationNotes: The chosen representative of the limit process is required to have continuous paths everywhere, and its designated maximizer must belong to the limit set and be unique pointwise. This is stronger than an almost-sure reading. Sample paths are assumed bounded on each compact set; limit boundedness follows from continuity and compactness.

title: Differentiability in Quadratic Mean
informal: A parametric model $M$ is differentiable in quadratic mean at $\theta$ with score $\ell$ relative to the dominating measure $\mu$ if the Hellinger residual lies in $L^2(\mu)$ for $h$ near $0$ and the square-root densities admit the $L^2(\mu)$ expansion $$\int\Big(\sqrt{p_{\theta+h}}-\sqrt{p_\theta}-\tfrac12\langle h,\ell\rangle\sqrt{p_\theta}\Big)^2\,d\mu = o(\|h\|^2)$$ as $h\to0$.
summary: A parametric model is differentiable in quadratic mean at theta with score ell when the Hellinger residual of the square-root densities is o-of-norm-h-squared in L2.
leanSignature:
structure DifferentiableQuadraticMean
    (M : ParametricFamily 𝓧 Θ) (μ : Measure 𝓧) (θ : Θ)
    (ℓ : 𝓧 → Θ) : Prop where
  mem : ∀ᶠ h in 𝓝 (0 : Θ),
    MemLp (fun x => M.sqrtDensity (θ + h) x - M.sqrtDensity θ x
                    - (1/2 : ℝ) * ⟪h, ℓ x⟫ * M.sqrtDensity θ x) 2 μ
  isLittleO :
    (fun h : Θ =>
      ∫ x, (M.sqrtDensity (θ + h) x
            - M.sqrtDensity θ x
            - (1/2 : ℝ) * ⟪h, ℓ x⟫ * M.sqrtDensity θ x) ^ 2 ∂μ)
    =o[𝓝 (0 : Θ)] (fun h : Θ => ‖h‖ ^ 2)
formalizationNotes: The displayed integral is accompanied by an explicit local square-integrability requirement. This excludes the convention under which a non-integrable Bochner integral is assigned zero and makes the definition equivalent to the usual Lebesgue-integral formulation.

hypotheses.label: square-integrable residual
hypotheses.note: The Hellinger residual √p_{θ+h} − √p_θ − ½⟨h, ℓ⟩√p_θ is square-integrable against μ for every h in a neighbourhood of 0, so the displayed integral is finite.

hypotheses.label: o(‖h‖²) rate
hypotheses.note: The integrated squared Hellinger residual is of smaller order than ‖h‖² as h → 0.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: The quadratic-mean differentiability formulation is central to L. Le Cam's theory of locally asymptotically normal experiments.

title: Quadratic-Mean-Differentiable Path
informal: A dominated quadratic-mean-differentiable path at a probability measure $P$ is a curve $t\mapsto Q_t$ of probability measures with $Q_0=P$, each dominated by a fixed $\sigma$-finite measure $\mu$, together with a score $g\in L^2_0(P)$ (mean zero, square-integrable) such that $$\big\|\sqrt{p_t}-\sqrt{p_0}-\tfrac{t}{2}\,g\,\sqrt{p_0}\big\|_{L^2(\mu)}\big/|t|\to0$$ as $t\to0$, where the densities $p_t$ are Radon–Nikodym derivatives of $Q_t$ with respect to $\mu$.
summary: A curve of probability measures through P, dominated by a fixed measure, with an L2-zero-mean score whose half is the L2 derivative of the square-root density.
leanSignature:
structure QMDPath (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P] where
  curve : ℝ → Measure Ω
  curve_at_zero : curve 0 = P
  curve_isProbability : ∀ t, IsProbabilityMeasure (curve t)
  dominating : Measure Ω
  curve_absContinuous : ∀ t, curve t ≪ dominating
  dominating_sigmaFinite : SigmaFinite dominating
  score : ↥(L2ZeroMean P)
  qmd_limit :
    Tendsto
      (fun t : ℝ =>
        eLpNorm (fun ω : Ω =>
          Real.sqrt ((curve t).rnDeriv dominating ω).toReal
            - Real.sqrt ((curve 0).rnDeriv dominating ω).toReal
            - (t / 2) * (score : Ω → ℝ) ω
                * Real.sqrt ((curve 0).rnDeriv dominating ω).toReal)
          2 dominating / ENNReal.ofReal |t|)
      (𝓝[≠] 0) (𝓝 (0 : ℝ≥0∞))
formalizationNotes: This is the dominated specialization: one sigma-finite measure dominates the full curve, and the score is required to be mean-zero and square-integrable under $P$. The extended-nonnegative norm quotient ensures the residual is genuinely square-integrable near zero.

hypotheses.label: quadratic-mean limit
hypotheses.note: The L²(μ) norm of the square-root-density residual, divided by |t|, tends to 0 as t → 0.

hypotheses.label: passes through P
hypotheses.note: The curve of probability measures equals P at t = 0.

hypotheses.label: common dominating measure
hypotheses.note: Every measure on the curve is absolutely continuous with respect to the fixed σ-finite measure μ.

hypotheses.label: mean-zero square-integrable score
hypotheses.note: The score g has mean zero and finite second moment under P.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: Quadratic-mean differentiable paths are part of L. Le Cam's local asymptotic theory.

title: Regular Estimator Sequence
informal: An estimator sequence $T_n$ for $\psi(\theta)$ is regular at $\theta_0$ if there exists a limit probability measure $L_\theta$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ such that for every $h\in\mathbb{R}^k$, $$\sqrt n\,\big(T_n-\psi(\theta_0+h/\sqrt n)\big)\xrightarrow{P^n_{\theta_0+h/\sqrt n}} L_\theta,$$ with the limit $L_\theta$ the same for every $h$. The independence of $L_\theta$ from $h$ is the regularity requirement.
summary: An estimator sequence whose rescaled recentred statistic converges weakly to one common h-independent limit law under each local alternative.
leanSignature:
structure RegularEstimatorSequence
    (M : ParametricFamily 𝓧 (AsymptoticRepresentation.Θ k)) (μ : Measure 𝓧)
    (θ₀ : AsymptoticRepresentation.Θ k)
    (ψ : AsymptoticRepresentation.Θ k → AsymptoticRepresentation.𝓨 d)
    (T : ∀ n, (Fin n → 𝓧) → AsymptoticRepresentation.𝓨 d) : Type where
  limitDist : Measure (AsymptoticRepresentation.𝓨 d)
  isProb : IsProbabilityMeasure limitDist
  tendsto : ∀ h : AsymptoticRepresentation.Θ k,
    WeakConverges
      (fun n : ℕ =>
        (AsymptoticRepresentation.productMeasure M μ (θ₀ + (Real.sqrt n)⁻¹ • h) n).map
          (fun x => (Real.sqrt n) •
            (T n x - ψ (θ₀ + (Real.sqrt n)⁻¹ • h))))
      limitDist
formalizationNotes: The common limit is required to be a probability measure and weak convergence is expressed through bounded continuous test functions. Unlike the book's usual use of ‘estimator’, this definition does not itself require measurability of $T_n$; the theorems that use it impose measurability separately.

hypotheses.label: shift-invariant weak limit
hypotheses.note: For every h, √n(T_n − ψ(θ₀ + h/√n)) converges weakly under the local alternative to the limit law.

hypotheses.label: common limit law
hypotheses.note: One limit distribution L_θ serves for every h; that independence of h is exactly regularity.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: The regular-estimator concept and its convolution theorem originate with J. Hájek, "A characterization of limiting distributions of regular estimates," *Zeitschrift für Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie und Verwandte Gebiete* **14** (1970), 323–330, with an independent treatment by T. Inagaki in 1970 and a decision-theoretic development by L. Le Cam in 1986.

title: Bowl-Shaped Loss Function
informal: A loss function $L:E\to[0,\infty]$ is bowl-shaped if it is measurable, symmetric about the origin ($L(-x)=L(x)$), and has convex sublevel sets $\{x : L(x)\le c\}$.
summary: A measurable, origin-symmetric loss with convex sublevel sets; the standing loss assumption for the local asymptotic minimax theorem.
leanSignature:
structure BowlShaped [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E]
    (L : E → ℝ≥0∞) : Prop where
  measurable : Measurable L
  symm : ∀ x, L (-x) = L x
  convex_sublevel : ∀ c : ℝ≥0∞, Convex ℝ {x | L x ≤ c}
formalizationNotes: The definition also requires measurability, which is needed for risks, and allows the extended value $+\infty$. Lower semicontinuity is not part of bowl-shapedness; adding it gives the closed-sublevel (‘subconvex’) case.

hypotheses.label: measurability
hypotheses.note: L is measurable, so its integrals against the candidate limit laws are defined.

hypotheses.label: symmetry
hypotheses.note: L is symmetric about the origin: L(−x) = L(x).

hypotheses.label: convex sublevel sets
hypotheses.note: Every sublevel set {x : L(x) ≤ c} is convex; with symmetry these are convex symmetric sets.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.

title: Gaussian Shift Experiment
informal: The Gaussian shift experiment with covariance $\Sigma$ is the family of laws on $\mathbb R^k$ indexed by a shift $h\in\mathbb R^k$ whose $h$-th member is a Gaussian probability measure with mean $h$, i.e. $\int\langle u,x\rangle\,dN(h,\Sigma)(x)=\langle u,h\rangle$ for every $u$ and covariance $\Sigma$, i.e. $\int\langle u,x-h\rangle\langle w,x-h\rangle\,dN(h,\Sigma)(x)=\langle u,\Sigma w\rangle$ for all $u,w$, where $\Sigma$ is positive definite. In short, the $h$-th member is $N(h,\Sigma)$.
summary: The family h to N(h, Sigma) of Gaussian probability measures with mean h and fixed positive-definite covariance Sigma, the limit experiment of local asymptotic normality.
leanSignature:
structure IsGaussianShift
    (family : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)))
    (cov : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ) : Prop where
  posDef : Matrix.PosDef cov
  isProb : ∀ h, IsProbabilityMeasure (family h)
  isGaussian : ∀ h, IsGaussian (family h)
  mean_eq (h u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)) :
    (∫ x, ⟪u, x⟫ ∂(family h)) = ⟪u, h⟫
  cov_eq (h u v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)) :
    (∫ x, ⟪u, x - h⟫ * ⟪v, x - h⟫ ∂(family h)) =
      ⟪u, (WithLp.equiv 2 _).symm (cov.mulVec ((WithLp.equiv 2 _) v))⟫
formalizationNotes: The definition records separately that every member is a probability law, is Gaussian, has mean equal to its shift, and has the common covariance. The affine log-likelihood-ratio identity is a separate property of the shift experiment.

hypotheses.label: positive definite covariance
hypotheses.note: The covariance matrix Σ is positive definite, so the shift experiment is nondegenerate.

hypotheses.label: Gaussian members
hypotheses.note: Each member of the family is a Gaussian probability measure.

hypotheses.label: mean equals the shift
hypotheses.note: The member indexed by h has mean h, stated through ∫⟨u, x⟩ = ⟨u, h⟩ for every u.

hypotheses.label: common covariance
hypotheses.note: Every member has the same covariance Σ, stated through the centred bilinear integral.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: The Gaussian shift experiment is the canonical limit experiment of L. Le Cam's local asymptotic theory; see his 1960 paper on locally asymptotically normal families and his 1986 monograph on statistical decision theory.

title: Equivariant-in-Law Estimator
informal: A randomized estimator $T$ of $A\cdot h$ in the Gaussian shift experiment, encoded as a Markov kernel $\mathbb{R}^k\rightsquigarrow\mathbb{R}^d$, is equivariant-in-law if for every $h$, the distribution of $T(X)-A\cdot h$ under $X\sim N(h,S)$ equals one common probability measure $L$ — i.e. the law of $T-Ah$ does not depend on $h$. That common $L$ is the null distribution of $T$.
summary: A randomized estimator (Markov kernel) whose centred law T(X) − Ah under N(h,S) is the same probability measure for every shift h.
leanSignature:
structure IsEquivariantInLaw
    (T : Kernel (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)) (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)))
    (A : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin k) ℝ)
    (S : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ) : Prop where
  invariant_law :
    ∃ L : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)),
      IsProbabilityMeasure L ∧
      ∀ h : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k),
        (T ∘ₘ (multivariateGaussian h S)).map
            (fun y => y - (WithLp.equiv 2 (Fin d → ℝ)).symm
              (A.mulVec ((WithLp.equiv 2 (Fin k → ℝ)) h)))
          = L
formalizationNotes: A single Markov kernel represents the randomized estimator. After centering its output by the transformed shift, the resulting law is one probability measure independent of the shift; $S$ denotes the Gaussian covariance.

hypotheses.label: shift-invariant centred law
hypotheses.note: One probability measure L equals the law of T(X) − Ah when X is drawn from N(h, S), simultaneously for every shift h.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: The convolution structure for regular equivariant limits originates with J. Hájek and was developed independently by L. Le Cam and T. Inagaki.

title: Parametric Submodel is Differentiable in Quadratic Mean
informal: The finite-dimensional parametric submodel constructed from a bounded family of mixture scores $g_P$ that are orthonormal in $L^2(P)$ is differentiable in quadratic mean at $\theta=0$ with multi-dimensional score $g_{P,\text{total}}$: the integrated squared Hellinger residual $\int\big(\sqrt{p_\theta}-1-\tfrac12\langle\theta,g_{P,\text{total}}\rangle\big)^2$ is $o(\|\theta\|^2)$ as $\theta\to0$.
summary: The submodel built from bounded orthonormal mixture scores is differentiable in quadratic mean at zero with score g_P_total.
leanSignature:
theorem paramSubmodel_DQM :
    DifferentiableQuadraticMean (paramSubmodel g_P hg h_orth) P 0 (g_P_total g_P)
formalizationNotes: A finite-dimensional submodel is constructed from bounded orthonormal score directions. It is differentiable in quadratic mean at zero; a fourth-order bound on the integrated squared residual is therefore little-o of the squared parameter norm.

hypotheses.label: bounded score directions
hypotheses.note: The submodel is the mixture family built from the uniformly bounded score directions g_P.

hypotheses.label: orthonormal scores
hypotheses.note: The score directions are orthonormal in L²(P), which makes the Fisher information of the submodel the identity.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.

title: Local Asymptotic Normality Expansion
informal: Let $(P_\theta)$ be a parametric family that is differentiable in quadratic mean at $\theta_0$ with measurable score $\ell$, with $p_\theta$ a genuine $\mu$-density for every $\theta$ (nonnegative, integrable, integrating to $1$), and let $X_i$ be i.i.d. with law $P_{\theta_0}$. Then for any $h_n\to h$ the score has zero mean, the Fisher information $\langle h,I_{\theta_0}h\rangle$ is finite in every direction, and the log-likelihood ratio admits the expansion $$\log\prod_{i\le n}\frac{p_{\theta_0+h_n/\sqrt n}(X_i)}{p_{\theta_0}(X_i)}=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i\le n}\langle h,\ell(X_i)\rangle-\tfrac12\langle h,I_{\theta_0}h\rangle+o_P(1).$$

hypotheses.note: Each p_θ is a nonnegative integrable μ-density integrating to 1.

hypotheses.label: differentiability in quadratic mean
hypotheses.note: The family is differentiable in quadratic mean at θ₀ with a measurable score ℓ.

hypotheses.label: converging local parameter
hypotheses.note: The local parameter sequence h_n converges to h.

hypotheses.label: i.i.d. sample at the truth

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.

title: Asymptotic Representation Theorem (LAN)
informal: Assume the family is differentiable in quadratic mean at $\theta_0$ with score $\ell$, with nonsingular Fisher information $J$ and $p_\theta$ a genuine $\mu$-density for every $\theta$, and that a statistic sequence $T_n$ converges weakly to a law $L_h$ under each local alternative $P^n_{\theta_0+h/\sqrt n}$. Then there exists a single Markov kernel $\kappa$ from $\mathbb R^k$ to the sample space of $T_n$ such that, for every $h$, $$L_h(B)=\int\kappa(z,B)\,dN\bigl(h,J^{-1}\bigr)(z);$$ that is, every limit law is obtained by drawing $Z\sim N(h,J^{-1})$ in the Gaussian shift experiment and then randomizing through one fixed kernel. Nothing the statistic can do in the limit exceeds what the Gaussian shift experiment allows.
summary: Under DQM with nonsingular Fisher information, the local limit laws of a weakly converging statistic sequence are obtained by applying one common Markov kernel to the corresponding Gaussian-shift laws.
leanSignature:
theorem LAN_representation
    (M : ParametricFamily 𝓧 (Θ k)) (μ : Measure 𝓧) [SigmaFinite μ]
    (θ₀ : Θ k) (ℓ : 𝓧 → Θ k) (hℓ : Measurable ℓ)
    (hDQM : DifferentiableQuadraticMean M μ θ₀ ℓ)
    (J : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ) (hJ_pd : Matrix.PosDef J)
    (hJ : ∀ u v : Θ k, fisherInformation M μ θ₀ ℓ u v =
      ⟪u, (WithLp.equiv 2 _).symm (J.mulVec ((WithLp.equiv 2 _) v))⟫)
    (T : ∀ n, (Fin n → 𝓧) → 𝓨 d) (hT_meas : ∀ n, Measurable (T n))
    (L : Θ k → Measure (𝓨 d)) [∀ h, IsProbabilityMeasure (L h)]
    (hT_weak : ∀ h : Θ k,
      WeakConverges
        (fun n => (productMeasure M μ (θ₀ + (Real.sqrt n)⁻¹ • h) n).map (T n)) (L h))
    [StandardBorelSpace (𝓨 d)] [Nonempty (𝓨 d)]
    [HasOuterApproxClosed (𝓨 d)] [BorelSpace (𝓨 d)]
    (hPDF : IsPDFOf M μ) :
    ∃ κ : Kernel (Θ k) (𝓨 d), IsMarkovKernel κ ∧
      ∀ h : Θ k, L h = (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian h J⁻¹).bind κ
formalizationNotes: The theorem gives the Markov-kernel representation of every local weak limit as a Gaussian shift followed by one common randomization kernel. Quadratic-mean differentiability controls asymptotically singular mass, so exact common support is not assumed.

hypotheses.label: differentiability in quadratic mean
hypotheses.note: The family is differentiable in quadratic mean at θ₀ with score ℓ.

hypotheses.label: nonsingular Fisher information
hypotheses.note: The Fisher information matrix J is positive definite.

hypotheses.label: weak convergence under local alternatives
hypotheses.note: The statistic sequence converges weakly to a law L_h under each local alternative.

hypotheses.label: one randomization kernel
hypotheses.note: A single Markov kernel realises every limit law as a randomization of the Gaussian shift N(h, J⁻¹).

hypotheses.label: genuine densities
hypotheses.note: Each p_θ is a nonnegative integrable μ-density integrating to 1.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: The result and the surrounding theory of *limit experiments* originate with L. Le Cam, "Limits of experiments," *Proceedings of the Sixth Berkeley Symposium on Mathematical Statistics and Probability*, Vol. I, University of California Press, 1972, pp. 245–261. Closely related convolution- and representation-theorem ideas were pioneered concurrently by J. Hájek, "Local asymptotic minimax and admissibility in estimation," same Proceedings (Vol. I, pp. 175–194, 1972), and later extended by A. W. van der Vaart, "An asymptotic representation theorem," *International Statistical Review* **59** (1991), 97–121.

title: Hájek–Le Cam Convolution Theorem
informal: Suppose the experiment is differentiable in quadratic mean at $\theta_0$ with score $\ell$ and has nonsingular Fisher information $J$, the target functional $\psi$ is Fréchet differentiable at $\theta_0$ with derivative $\dot\psi$, and $T_n$ is a regular estimator sequence for $\psi(\theta)$, i.e. $\sqrt n(T_n-\psi(\theta_0+h/\sqrt n))$ converges weakly to one $h$-independent law $L_\theta$ under every local alternative. Then there is a probability measure $M_\theta$ with $$L_\theta=N\bigl(0,\ \dot\psi\,J^{-1}\,\dot\psi^{\mathsf T}\bigr)*M_\theta,$$ so the limit law of any regular estimator is the optimal Gaussian law convolved with extra noise; the Gaussian alone is the best attainable limit.
summary: The limit law of any regular estimator of psi factors as the convolution of the optimal Gaussian N(0, psidot J-inverse psidot-transpose) with some probability measure.
leanSignature:

    (M : ParametricFamily 𝓧 (Θ k)) (μ : Measure 𝓧) [SigmaFinite μ]
    (θ₀ : Θ k) (ℓ : 𝓧 → Θ k) (hℓ : Measurable ℓ)
    (hDQM : DifferentiableQuadraticMean M μ θ₀ ℓ)
    (J : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ) (hJ_pd : Matrix.PosDef J)
    (hJ_fisher : ∀ u v : Θ k, fisherInformation M μ θ₀ ℓ u v =
      ⟪u, (WithLp.equiv 2 _).symm (J.mulVec ((WithLp.equiv 2 _) v))⟫)

title: Local Asymptotic Minimax Bound
informal: Suppose a normalized density model is differentiable in quadratic mean at $\theta_0$ with a measurable score $\ell$, $J$ is the actual Fisher information matrix and is positive definite, the functional $\psi$ is Fréchet differentiable at $\theta_0$ with derivative $\dot\psi$, the loss $L$ is lower semicontinuous and bowl-shaped, and the measurable rescaled estimators are uniformly tight at the truth. Then $$\sup_{I\subset\mathbb R^k, I\text{ finite}}\liminf_{n\to\infty}\sup_{h\in I}\mathbb E_{P^n_{\theta_0+h/\sqrt n}}\!\left[L\!\left(\sqrt n\bigl(T_n-\psi(\theta_0+h/\sqrt n)\bigr)\right)\right]\ge\int L\,dN\!\left(0,\dot\psi J^{-1}\dot\psi^{\mathsf T}\right).$$

title: Tangent set / tangent space
informal: At a probability measure $P$, a tangent set is a collection of mean-zero square-integrable functions in $L^2_0(P)$, each of which is the score of a submodel through $P$. Formally it consists of a set of admissible score directions inside $L^2_0(P)$ together with, for every direction $g$ in that set, a quadratic-mean-differentiable curve $t\mapsto Q_t$ with $Q_0=P$ whose score is exactly $g$. The closed linear span of a tangent set is the tangent space; it plays the role of the parameter space of the local Gaussian experiment.
summary: A tangent set is a set of QMD-realizable score directions in L²₀(P); its closed linear span is the tangent space.
leanSignature:
structure TangentSpec (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P] where
  carrier : Set ↥(L2ZeroMean P)
  submodelOf : ∀ g ∈ carrier, ∃ γ : AsymptoticStatistics.Core.QMDPath.QMDPath P,
    γ.score = g
formalizationNotes: The carrier is a set of mean-zero square-integrable score directions. Every direction in it must be realized by a quadratic-mean-differentiable probability curve through the reference law.

hypotheses.label: set of score directions
hypotheses.note: The tangent set proper: a set of mean-zero square-integrable functions.

title: Regular estimator (semiparametric)
informal: Let $\psi$ be a scalar functional of the underlying law, differentiable along the tangent space at $P$ with derivative $d\psi$, and let $\tilde\psi_P$ be an efficient influence function for $d\psi$, i.e. an element of the tangent space with $d\psi(g)=\langle\tilde\psi_P,g\rangle$ for every tangent direction $g$. A sequence $T_n$ of estimators is regular at $P$ relative to the tangent set with limit law $L$ if, for every direction $g$ in the linear span of the tangent set and every quadratic-mean-differentiable curve through $P$ whose score is $g$, the rescaled estimator recentred at the perturbed truth has the same weak limit: $$\sqrt n\,\bigl(T_n-\psi(P_{1/\sqrt n,\,g})\bigr)\rightsquigarrow L\qquad\text{under }P^n_{1/\sqrt n,\,g},$$ with $L$ not depending on $g$. This shift-invariance is what rules out estimators that are superefficient at $P$ at the cost of erratic behaviour nearby.
summary: An estimator is regular if the perturbed-truth-recentered rescaled statistic has the same weak limit L along every QMD score direction.
leanSignature:
def IsRegularEstimator
    (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (T_set : TangentSpec P)
    (ψ : Measure Ω → ℝ)
    {IF_eff : ↥(L2ZeroMean P)}
    (hψ : PathwiseDifferentiableAt P (tangentSpace T_set) ψ)
    (_hEIF : IsEfficientInfluenceFunction P (tangentSpace T_set)
              hψ.derivative IF_eff)
    (T_n : ∀ n, (Fin n → Ω) → ℝ)
    (L : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure L] : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : ↥(L2ZeroMean P))
    (_hg : (g : ↥(L2ZeroMean P)) ∈ Submodule.span ℝ T_set.carrier)
    (curve : QMDPath P)
    (_hscore : curve.score = g),
    WeakConverges
      (fun n : ℕ =>
        (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi
            (fun _ : Fin n => curve.curve ((Real.sqrt n)⁻¹))).map
          (fun X : Fin n → Ω =>
            Real.sqrt n *
              (T_n n X - ψ (curve.curve ((Real.sqrt n)⁻¹)))))
      L
formalizationNotes: The definition requires one common probability limit along every realized direction in the linear span of the tangent set. The supplied pathwise derivative and efficient influence function identify the statistical setting but are not used inside this regularity predicate.

title: Coarsening-at-Random Family
informal: A differentiable conditional-law family satisfies coarsening at random relative to an observation map $M$ if for every path value $t$, its conditional density is measurable, almost everywhere, with respect to the sigma-algebra generated by $M$. Thus the conditional density depends on the full data only through the observed value.
summary: A conditional-law path is coarsening at random when each conditional density is measurable through the observation map.
leanSignature:
def IsCARFamily (M : 𝓨 × 𝓓 → 𝓧) (γ : ConditionalQMDPath Q ν r) : Prop :=
  ∀ t : ℝ,
    AEStronglyMeasurable[MeasurableSpace.comap M ‹MeasurableSpace 𝓧›]
      (fun p : 𝓨 × 𝓓 => ((γ.curve t p.1).rnDeriv ν p.2).toReal) (Q.prod ν)
formalizationNotes: This is the family-level coarsening-at-random restriction: it applies to every member of the differentiable conditional-law path, rather than to one fixed measure.

hypotheses.note: For every path value, the conditional density is almost everywhere measurable with respect to the sigma-algebra generated by the observation map.

title: Nondominated QMD Score and LAN Expansion
informal: Let a one-sided curve consist of probability measures for nonnegative times, pass through $P$ at zero, and let $g$ be measurable. If the curve is right-differentiable in quadratic mean at zero with score $g$, and if the sample coordinates are measurable, independent, identically distributed, and have common law $P$, then $g$ has mean zero and a finite second moment under $P$, and the local log-likelihood ratio has the usual local asymptotic normal expansion with score $g$.

theorem qmd_score_mean_integrable_and_lan_nondominated
    (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (curve : ℝ → Measure Ω)
    (hprob : ∀ t, 0 ≤ t → IsProbabilityMeasure (curve t))
    (hzero : curve 0 = P)
    (g : Ω → ℝ) (hg : Measurable g)
    (hqmd : IsRightQMD P curve g)
    (P' : Measure Ω') [IsProbabilityMeasure P']
    (X : ℕ → Ω' → Ω) (hX_meas : ∀ i, Measurable (X i))
    (hindep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X P')
    (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) P' P')
    (hlaw : Measure.map (X 0) P' = P) :
    (∫ ω, g ω ∂P = 0) ∧ Integrable (fun ω => g ω ^ 2) P ∧
      TendstoInMeasure P'
        (fun n ω =>
          (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n,
            Real.log (((curve ((Real.sqrt n)⁻¹)).rnDeriv P (X i ω)).toReal))
            - (Real.sqrt n)⁻¹ * ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, g (X i ω)
            + (1 / 2 : ℝ) * ∫ x, g x ^ 2 ∂P)

title: EIF as orthogonal projection of an influence function
informal: For a continuous linear derivative $d\psi:T\to\mathbb R$, let $\mathrm{IF}$ be any influence function representing $d\psi$ on the tangent space $T$. The residual is orthogonal to every tangent direction, so projection preserves the derivative representation while placing the representer in $T$.

title: Operational efficiency bound (sup-ratio form)
informal: The supremum over the tangent space of the squared inner-product ratio equals the squared norm of the efficient influence function, $$\sup_{g \in T} \frac{\langle \tilde\psi_P, g\rangle^2}{\|g\|^2} = \|\tilde\psi_P\|^2.$$ The upper bound is Cauchy–Schwarz term-by-term; equality is attained at $g = \tilde\psi_P$, which lies in the tangent space $T$.

title: Semiparametric convolution theorem (scalar)
informal: Let a scalar functional be pathwise differentiable along a tangent set, with an efficient influence function representing its derivative. Let $T_n$ be measurable, and suppose $T_n$ is regular with common limit law $L$ along every tangent direction, where $L$ has a finite second moment. Then the variance of $L$ is at least the squared norm of the efficient influence function. If the tangent set is a convex cone, $L$ is the convolution of the corresponding centered Gaussian law with another probability measure.
summary: For a regular estimator, the asymptotic variance is at least ‖ψ̃‖² and (over a convex cone) the limit law is N(0,‖ψ̃‖²) convolved with a residual.
leanSignature:
theorem semiparametric_convolution_theorem
    (T_set : TangentSpec P)
    {ψ : Measure Ω → ℝ}
    (hψ : PathwiseDifferentiableAt P (tangentSpace T_set) ψ)
    {IF_eff : ↥(L2ZeroMean P)}
    (hEIF : IsEfficientInfluenceFunction P (tangentSpace T_set)
              hψ.derivative IF_eff)
    (T_n : ∀ n, (Fin n → Ω) → ℝ)
    (hT_meas : ∀ n, Measurable (T_n n))
    (L : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure L]
    (hReg : AsymptoticStatistics.LowerBounds.RegularEstimator.IsRegularEstimator
              P T_set ψ hψ hEIF T_n L)
    (hL_memLp : MeasureTheory.MemLp (id : ℝ → ℝ) 2 L) :
    ‖(IF_eff : ↥(L2ZeroMean P))‖ ^ 2 ≤ (∫ x, (x - ∫ y, y ∂L)^2 ∂L) ∧
    ((∀ x ∈ T_set.carrier, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t • x ∈ T_set.carrier) →
     (∀ x ∈ T_set.carrier, ∀ y ∈ T_set.carrier,
        ∀ a b : ℝ, 0 ≤ a → 0 ≤ b → a + b = 1 →
        a • x + b • y ∈ T_set.carrier) →
     let sigma_sq : ℝ≥0 :=
       ⟨‖(IF_eff : ↥(L2ZeroMean P))‖ ^ 2, sq_nonneg _⟩
     ∃ M : Measure ℝ, IsProbabilityMeasure M ∧
       L = MeasureTheory.Measure.conv
              (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 sigma_sq) M)
formalizationNotes: The variance bound uses the finite second moment explicitly. The Gaussian convolution conclusion is conditional on the tangent carrier being both a cone and convex.

title: Semiparametric convolution theorem (vector)
informal: Let $\psi$ be a vector-valued functional that is pathwise differentiable, with a tuple of efficient influence functions representing its coordinate derivatives. Let $T_n$ be measurable, suppose $T_n$ is regular with common vector limit law $L$, and assume $L$ has finite second moments. Then the covariance of $L$ dominates the Gram matrix of the efficient influence tuple, and $L$ is the convolution of the centered Gaussian law with that Gram covariance and another probability law.

theorem semiparametric_convolution_theorem_vec

    (hψ : PathwiseDifferentiableAt_vec P (tangentSpace T_set) ψ)
    {IF_eff : Fin k → ↥(L2ZeroMean P)}
    (hEIF : IsEfficientInfluenceFunction_vec hψ.derivative IF_eff)
    (T_n : ∀ n, (Fin n → Ω) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k))
    (hT_meas : ∀ n, Measurable (T_n n))
    (L : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k))) [IsProbabilityMeasure L]
    (hReg : IsRegularEstimator_vec P T_set ψ hψ hEIF T_n L)
    (hL_memLp : MemLp (id : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) → _) 2 L) :
    let G : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ := Matrix.gram ℝ IF_eff
    let Sigma : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ := fun i j =>
      ∫ y, (y.ofLp i - ∫ z, z.ofLp i ∂L)
          * (y.ofLp j - ∫ z, z.ofLp j ∂L) ∂L

    (∃ M : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)), IsProbabilityMeasure M ∧

title: Nondominated Semiparametric Local Asymptotic Minimax Theorem
informal: Let the selected nondominated tangent carrier be convex, let a vector functional be pathwise differentiable along the selected paths, and let an efficient influence tuple represent its derivative. title: Scalar LAM under linear-tangent and tightness assumptions
informal: Let a tangent carrier be closed under nonnegative scaling, convex combinations, and negation, and assume it is nonempty. Suppose the scalar functional is pathwise differentiable, its derivative has an efficient influence function, and the estimator sequence is measurable. Let the loss be bowl-shaped, with every finite truncation lower semicontinuous, and assume the rescaled estimators are tight at the truth. Then the finite-direction local asymptotic risk is bounded below by the corresponding centered Gaussian risk.
summary: Scalar case: the local minimax risk for a subconvex loss is at least its integral against N(0, ‖ψ̃‖²).

title: Operational Efficiency Characterization, Nondominated Form

title: EIF from the efficient score
informal: The efficient score $\tilde\ell_v$ in direction $v$ is the ordinary score $S_\theta v$ minus its orthogonal projection onto the nuisance tangent space; the efficient information is $\tilde I(v) = \|\tilde\ell_v\|^2$. the normalized efficient score $\tfrac{1}{\tilde I(v)}\,\tilde\ell_v$ is an efficient influence function for the linear-functional derivative $d\psi$, provided the candidate lies in the target tangent space and $d\psi$ acts on $T$ as $\tfrac{1}{\tilde I(v)}\langle \tilde\ell_v, \cdot\rangle$.
summary: The normalized efficient score (1/Ï) · ℓ̃_v is an efficient influence function for the corresponding linear functional of θ.

    (h_mem :
      (1 / efficientInformation S_θ T_nuis v)
        • efficientScore S_θ T_nuis v ∈ T)
    (dψ : T →L[ℝ] ℝ)
    (h_dψ : ∀ g : T,
      dψ g
        = (1 / efficientInformation S_θ T_nuis v)
            * ⟪efficientScore S_θ T_nuis v, (g : ↥(L2ZeroMean P))⟫_ℝ) :
    IsEfficientInfluenceFunction P T dψ
      ((1 / efficientInformation S_θ T_nuis v)
        • efficientScore S_θ T_nuis v)

It does not construct a realizing path or infer nonsingularity. Zero information is permitted only when the supplied membership and representation make the zero candidate an efficient influence function.

title: EIF via the information operator
informal: Let $A$ be a score operator. Suppose $\kappa$ solves the information equation $\langle A\kappa,Av\rangle=\langle\chi,v\rangle$ for every $v$, $A\kappa$ belongs to the tangent space $T$, every $g\in T$ is $Av$ for some $v$, and the derivative satisfies $d\psi(Av)=\langle\chi,v\rangle$ whenever $Av\in T$. Then $A\kappa$ is the efficient influence function for $d\psi$ on $T$.
summary: If κ solves the information equation ⟨Aκ, Av⟩ = ⟨χ, v⟩, then Aκ is the efficient influence function.

title: Efficient score as score-residual (semiparametric specialization)
informal: In a strict semiparametric model the score operator splits into a $\theta$-component $A_\theta$ and an $\eta$-component. The efficient score for the $\theta$-direction $v$ — the residual of the ordinary $\theta$-score $A_\theta v$ after projecting onto the $\eta$-tangent space $T_\eta$ — coincides with the abstract efficient score when the ordinary-score operator is taken to be $A_\theta$: $$A_\theta v - \Pi_{T_\eta}(A_\theta v) = \tilde\ell_v.$$
summary: The projection-residual of the θ-score onto the η-tangent space equals the abstract efficient score (definitionally).

    (v : H_θ) :
    A_θ.toCLM v - T_η.starProjection (A_θ.toCLM v)
      = AsymptoticStatistics.StrictModel.EfficientScore.efficientScore
          A_θ.toCLM T_η v

title: Actual and Maximal CAR Tangent Spaces
informal: For a sigma-finite reference measure $\nu$ on the coarsening variable, the observed scores of coarsening-at-random conditional paths lie in the intersection of the nuisance and concrete coarsening score spaces. Moreover, every centered square-integrable observed-data direction decomposes into an element of the closed observed full-data tangent space plus an orthogonal concrete coarsening score.

        carNuisanceScores Q r hM ν ⊓ concreteCoarseningScores Q r hM) ∧
    (∀ g : ↥(L2ZeroMean ((Q ⊗ₘ r).map M)),
      ∃ p ∈ (observedTangent hM (Q ⊗ₘ r) (fullQTangent Q r)).topologicalClosure,
        ∃ b ∈ concreteCoarseningScores Q r hM,

          ⟪(p : Lp ℝ 2 ((Q ⊗ₘ r).map M)),
            (b : Lp ℝ 2 ((Q ⊗ₘ r).map M))⟫_ℝ = 0)

title: Complete-Case IPW Influence Characterization
informal: Assume a complete-case value can be recovered from the observed data, choose $\varepsilon>0$, and suppose the selection probability is at least $\varepsilon$ almost everywhere. If $\chi$ is a full-data influence function and the observed derivative agrees with the full-data derivative on lifted full-data scores, then an observed-data function is an influence function exactly when it is the complete-case inverse-probability-weighted version of $\chi$ plus a concrete coarsening score.
summary: Observed influence functions form the affine space of the complete-case IPW base plus fibre-mean-zero coarsening scores.

    (h_mem : forall j,
      @candidateVecEIF Omega _ P _ Theta _ _ _ d S_theta T_nuis proj e j ∈ T)
    (h_Dpsi : forall (j : Fin d) (g : T),
      ((EuclideanSpace.proj j) ∘L Dpsi) g = inner Real
        (@candidateVecEIF Omega _ P _ Theta _ _ _ d S_theta T_nuis proj e j)
        (g : ↥(L2ZeroMean P)))
    {psi : Measure Omega -> EuclideanSpace Real (Fin d)} (hpsi : psi P = theta0) :
    SemiparametricallyEfficientAt_vec estimator psi P T
formalizationNotes: The hypotheses construct the proper approximate least-favorable submodel from probability laws and impose the score convergence, moving-bias, localization, consistency, and local likelihood-maximization conditions used in (25.75)–(25.76). They imply asymptotic linearity rather than assuming it. The vector conclusion uses the inverse of the full efficient-information matrix and therefore allows non-diagonal information.

title: Localized uniform-entropy modulus for Lipschitz classes
informal: Let every criterion function be measurable, let the Lipschitz envelope be square-integrable, and measurable, and suppose criterion differences are bounded pointwise by the envelope times parameter distance. If the observations are measurable, independent, identically distributed, and have common law $P$, then on a sufficiently small parameter ball the outer expected supremum of the centered empirical process is bounded by a constant times the ball radius, uniformly in the sample size.
summary: The empirical-process modulus of a finite-dimensional Lipschitz shell grows linearly with its radius, uniformly in sample size.
leanSignature:
theorem centeredLipschitz_localizedModulus_bound
    {d : ℕ} (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (m : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → Ω → ℝ) (θ₀ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (hm_meas : ∀ θ, Measurable (m θ))
    (menv : Ω → ℝ) (hmenv : MemLp menv 2 P) (hmenv_meas : Measurable menv)
    (hLip : ∀ θ₁ θ₂ ω, |m θ₁ ω - m θ₂ ω| ≤ menv ω * ‖θ₁ - θ₂‖)
    {Ξ : Type} [MeasurableSpace Ξ] (μ : Measure Ξ) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (X : ℕ → Ξ → Ω) (hX_meas : ∀ i, Measurable (X i))
    (hX_indep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ)
    (hX_id : ∀ i, ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ)
    (hX_law : μ.map (X 0) = P) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ ∧
      ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → δ < ρ → ∀ n : ℕ,
        ∫⁻ ξ, supNormOver
            {g : Ω → ℝ | ∃ θ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), ‖θ - θ₀‖ < δ ∧
              g = fun ω => m θ ω - m θ₀ ω}
            (fun f => empiricalProcess P n (fun i : Fin n => X i.val ξ) f) ∂μ
          ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * δ)
formalizationNotes: The formal statement uses a fixed-centre parameter shell. This is the form supported by the relative covering-number argument: a pairwise-difference slice has envelope $2M$ and does not supply the shell radius in the numerator of its covering estimate. The proof first treats the closed shell and then restricts to the open shell.

title: Efficient influence function for a mean under missing at random
informal: For a missing-at-random mean problem, assume the response kernel has propensity $\pi(X)$, $\pi$ never vanishes, the observed law has the stated propensity moments, the complete-case regression is $m(X)$, and the conditional Bernoulli variance identity holds. Suppose the efficient representer, the inverse-probability representer, the centered coarsening score, and the regression coarsening score are all square-integrable; assume $m(X)$ is integrable, $R/\pi(X)$ is integrable, $RY/\pi(X)$ is measurable, and $RY/\pi(X)$ is almost surely bounded by a finite constant. Under square-integrability of the augmented inverse-probability influence function, that augmented inverse-probability expression is the efficient influence function for the observed-data mean.
summary: The augmented inverse-probability formula is the efficient influence function for the bounded MAR mean functional.
leanSignature:
theorem marMean_isEIF
    (Q : Measure (X × ℝ)) [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]
    (r : Kernel (X × ℝ) Bool) [IsMarkovKernel r]
    (π m : X → ℝ)
    (hπr : MARResponseKernel π r)
    (hπ : ∀ o : MARObs X, π o.x ≠ 0)
    (hProp : MARPropensity π (marObsMeasure Q r))
    (hReg : MARRegression π m (marObsMeasure Q r))
    (hVar : MARVariance π (marObsMeasure Q r))
    (hLp : MemLp (marMean_eif π m (marMean_Ψ π (marObsMeasure Q r))) 2
      (marObsMeasure Q r))
    (hLp_ipw : MemLp (marMean_ipwRep π (marMean_Ψ π (marObsMeasure Q r))) 2
      (marObsMeasure Q r))
    (hLp_coar : MemLp
      (marMean_coarseningScore π (fun x => m x - marMean_Ψ π (marObsMeasure Q r))) 2
      (marObsMeasure Q r))
    (hLp_bm : MemLp (marMean_coarseningScore π m) 2 (marObsMeasure Q r))
    (hm_int : Integrable (fun o : MARObs X => m o.x) (marObsMeasure Q r))
    (hInt_weight : Integrable (fun o : MARObs X => ind o.r / π o.x) (marObsMeasure Q r))
    (h_ipwMeas : Measurable (fun o : MARObs X => ind o.r * o.ry / π o.x))
    (C : ℝ)
    (h_ipwBddAE : ∀ᵐ o ∂(marObsMeasure Q r), |ind o.r * o.ry / π o.x| ≤ C)
    :
    IsEfficientInfluenceFunction (marObsMeasure Q r) (marObservedTangent Q r)
      (marMeanBounded_pathwise π C h_ipwMeas (marObservedTangent Q r)).derivative
      (marMean_eifCandidate π m hπ hProp hLp hLp_ipw hLp_coar hm_int hInt_weight).toL2ZeroMean
formalizationNotes: The observed tangent space is constructed from the latent law and response kernel through the tangent characterization of Theorem 25.40, rather than supplied as a hypothesis. To control unrestricted QMD paths, the formalization differentiates a globally clipped extension of the inverse-probability mean. The almost-sure bound is stronger than the moment condition in Example 25.43; it makes the extension agree with the raw estimand at the model law while leaving the tangent identification independent of that bound.
